style.vernacular: Low-lying Atlantic-coast colonial capital laid out on a Dutch/British grid with drainage canals and kokers: ordinary buildings are Caribbean timber houses, often raised on stilts, painted white or pastel, with jalousie louvre windows, fretwork, gabled porches and corrugated zinc roofs; newer buildings are plain concrete-block boxes in painted render.
style.ornament: Timber fretwork and lattice, jalousie (louvre) windows and shutters, gabled porches and turrets, white-painted Gothic Revival and Victorian detailing, thatched benab huts echoing Amerindian building; seawall, canals and avenues lined with palms and flowering trees (the Garden City of the Caribbean).

sources.what: British and Dutch colonial influenced architecture, many wooden colonial buildings, canals and kokers, hot tropical climate, Garden City of the Caribbean
Gothic Revival timber construction as the signature building type
Victorian iron-and-steel market with clock tower
